title: Credit VaR and Granularity

maps.tested: Tested as a direct-formula computation and as a comparison against market-risk VaR on definition, horizon and toolset. The importance sheet singles out LO 30.g as the exam-relevant Credit VaR objective and warns against over-investing in the formulas of Reading 28 while still knowing all four models by name.
maps.specifics: Reported as 'CVaR calculation, direct formula application' and 'CVaR (1) FC'. Credit VaR = worst-case loss at the confidence level minus expected loss: the classic error is forgetting to subtract EL. Two granularity effects are separately examinable (LO 29.h): Credit VaR per unit of exposure falls as the portfolio becomes more granular, but does not fall to zero because of systematic correlation.

vardeezReading: CR-10: Very Important. "Credit Spread Risk can be imp too" (the comparison of the four credit risk models is also expected, but that belongs to topic D20). CR-11: Very Important, with LO 29.a, 29.c and 29.h the Very Important objectives; other objectives are not important. CR-12: Important. "LO30.g: This LO which talks abt Credit Var is imp for exam."

selectors.name: Credit VaR by direct formula
selectors.what: Credit VaR = quantile of the credit loss at the confidence level minus expected loss, with EL = sum of EAD x LGD x PD. Given the loss at the confidence level (for example from a binomial number of defaults times the loss per default) and the EL, compute Credit VaR; because EL is always subtracted, the result can be negative.
selectors.theory: What Credit VaR measures (Malz: the loss quantile minus the expected loss), why EL is deducted, why the 99% quantile is the smallest number of defaults whose cumulative probability reaches 99%, and how Hull's loss quantile L(1 - R) x WCDR differs because it does not deduct EL.

selectors.name: Trap: Credit VaR without subtracting EL
selectors.what: The formula-card form of S1: the option equal to the worst-case loss at the confidence level, with expected loss not deducted, sits among the answers; so can the twin built with the recovery rate in place of LGD.

selectors.name: Granularity effect 1: Credit VaR falls
selectors.what: For a given default probability, Credit VaR decreases as the portfolio becomes more granular (more, smaller credits); the fall is more drastic when the default probability is high and harder to achieve when it is low. Expected loss is unchanged by granularity.

selectors.name: Granularity effect 2: not zero when correlated
selectors.what: Credit VaR does not fall to zero as the portfolio becomes granular when defaults are correlated: idiosyncratic risk diversifies away but the systematic (market factor) risk remains. Only with independent defaults does the loss converge to EL and Credit VaR to zero. Correlation 1 behaves as n = 1, correlation 0 gives a binomial number of defaults.

selectors.name: Market VaR versus credit VaR
selectors.source: Map #10 tested: 'a comparison against market-risk VaR on definition, horizon and toolset' (LO 28.a)
selectors.what: Compare market risk VaR with credit VaR on definition (same concept; some credit models count only default losses, others also downgrades and spread changes), time horizon (market often one day, credit usually one year) and tools (historical simulation versus a more elaborate model).

selectors.name: Credit VaR via Gaussian copula, CreditMetrics
selectors.source: Map #10 tested: 'LO 30.g as the exam-relevant Credit VaR objective'; Vardeez: 'Credit VaR'
selectors.what: How Credit VaR is estimated with the Gaussian copula and the CreditMetrics approach: sample correlated normals, convert transition probabilities into thresholds, revalue every counterparty at the horizon, repeat, and read the quantile off the simulated losses.
